question: Why did Turkey ban sandblasting of denim in 2009?
answer: Workers were dying of silicosis. Blasting jeans with sand for a worn look filled small workshops with fine crystalline silica, which scars the lungs; young Turkish workers fell ill within a few years of starting, and some died. Big brands announced their own bans afterwards, and the work drifted to countries with weaker enforcement.
move: When a product looks worn for free, someone paid for the wear.

trap: EU rules: trade pressure seems the usual reason an industry changes method.
source: Akgun et al., European Respiratory Journal, 2008
reference: Akgun et al., An epidemic of silicosis among former denim sandblasters, European Respiratory Journal, 2008
